Visit note | 2026-03-05 03:00 PM | Dr. Anisur Rahman, Ophthalmology | Patient: Rashid Khan, 34, male. Mr. Khan presents with a painful red lump at the edge of his right eyelid along with noticeable swelling around the area. He mentions this appeared after using old eye makeup in Noakhali. He works as an office cleaner and has a history of Essential hypertension. He denies any visual disturbances, discharge, or prior eye surgeries. On examination: lump about 6 mm on the right upper eyelid, BP 146/87 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 66 kg. The conjunctiva is clear otherwise, and ocular motility is normal. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice provided: use a warm compress four times a day; do not squeeze the lump; avoid eye makeup. Follow-up: 1 week.

Visit note | 2026-03-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Hasan Dewan, 20, male. Mr. Dewan returns for review regarding his ongoing skin concerns, reporting marks left after pimples, persistent pimples and blackheads on his face, and spots on his back. He notes these symptoms became worse since working in a hot kitchen in Tejgaon. He works as a shopkeeper and has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. He denies using any unprescribed topical steroid creams. On examination: deep painful lumps along the jawline only, about 17 inflamed spots on the face, BP 120/78 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 61 kg. Visit note | 2026-03-05 03:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Hasina Mollah, 69, female. Mrs. Mollah attends a follow-up visit for her shoulder, stating she remains unable to reach behind her back and has experienced a stiff shoulder for weeks. Visit note | 2026-03-07 11:00 AM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Tapan Nath, 31, male. Mr. Nath presents to the clinic today complaining of bothersome belly cramps and a general sense of feeling very weak. He reports that these distressing gastrointestinal symptoms started shortly after drinking untreated tap water during a recent trip to Barishal. He works as a nurse in a local facility and reports no prior chronic medical conditions or regular medication use. He denies passing any blood or mucus in his stools, though he has experienced several loose bowel movements over the past twenty-four hours. He also denies any recent travel abroad or similar illness among close family members. Upon clinical examination today, his vital signs reveal a pulse rate of 113 bpm, blood pressure reading of 133/80 mmHg, and a body weight of 73 kg. Abdominal examination demonstrates mild, diffuse tenderness across the lower quadrants without any localized rigidity, guarding, or palpable organomegaly. Bowel sounds are notably hyperactive throughout all four quadrants. Cardiovascular and respiratory examinations are entirely unremarkable. Laboratory review and clinical evaluation support a diagnosis of acute infectious upset. Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis. Plan: a prescription was issued to manage symptoms and support rehydration. He was strongly advised to drink small sips of fluid often, consume bland foods such as rice, bananas, and toast, and maintain strict hand hygiene before eating. Follow-up: 2 days if the stools do not settle.
